A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same OmniVCus research work in 12 readable pages. Full-document text and rendering comparisons support reliable assessment of equations, figures, tables, and references. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v2.pdf reports original video-generation experiments, quantitative comparisons in Table 1, ablations in Table 2, and a user study with 37 participants.

after.justification: v3.pdf retains the original video-generation experiments, quantitative comparisons, ablations, and 37-participant user study in Section 4.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the identical VideoCus-Factory pipeline, OmniVCus architecture, Lottery Embedding, Temporally Aligned Embedding, IVTM training, and flow-matching objective.

E1.justification: Training sources and task coverage are identical, including Objaverse, OmniEdit, single- and multi-subject customization, instructive editing, camera/depth/mask controls, and texture-transfer scenarios.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains VideoBooth, DreamVideo, Wan2.1-I2V, and SkyReels-A2 for single-subject/editing comparisons, SkyReels-A2 for multi-subject comparisons, and Motionctrl, Cameractrl, and CamI2V for camera control. Their OmniGen preprocessing arrangements are unchanged.

E3.justification: Sections 4.1–4.2 retain identical training budgets, resolutions, evaluation sample counts, five evaluation metrics, multi-subject averaging procedures, and the 37-participant user-study protocol.

E4.justification: Table 2 and Figure 9 retain the same data-pipeline, TAE, LE, and IVTM ablations, including qualitative analyses of camera control, texture transfer, and subject preservation.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same point estimates and user-preference percentages. Neither reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–2 and qualitative results in Figures 1–9 are unchanged. For example, Table 1a retains OmniVCus single-subject CLIP-T of 0.3293 and DINO-I of 0.5215 under identical settings.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(3), the Lottery Embedding sampling definition, Plücker-coordinate representation, TAE mapping, and flow-matching formulation are identical. No theoretical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about data construction, zero-shot customization with more subjects, multimodal control, instructive editing, and superiority over evaluated methods.

C2.justification: The explanations of augmentation leakage, TAE control behavior, LE generalization, and IVTM transfer are unchanged. Discussions of misaligned control signals and failures of alternative configurations contain no new qualifications or limitations.

D1.justification: Both versions disclose the same augmentation ranges, 5B-parameter model, 64 A100 GPUs, optimizer and learning-rate settings, training schedule, and project-page access information.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, positioning against earlier customization methods, and all 78 reference entries are identical.

P1.justification: Only the first-page arXiv stamp changes from v2 dated 11 October 2025 to v3 dated 31 December 2025. The title, authors, prose, terminology, and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–9, Tables 1–2, captions, placement, and page layout are unchanged. Rendered pages are identical except for the first-page version/date stamp.

improvement.justification: The only visible revision is the arXiv version/date stamp. Scientific content, empirical evidence, explanations, reproducibility information, and document presentation are otherwise identical, establishing no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
